headline: Maine closes Casco Bay clam flats after bloom-linked die-off
dek: Emergency harvesting closures cover parts of Maquoit and Middle bays after severe stress and mortality among soft-shell clams; Brunswick says the bloom is a marine-life concern, not a shellfish-consumption toxin warning.
body: Maine regulators have closed shellfish harvesting in parts of Maquoit Bay and Middle Bay after local committees reported a die-off of soft-shell clams linked to a spreading phytoplankton bloom. Maine Public reported that the Department of Marine Resources ordered the closures in Brunswick and Harpswell after monitoring the affected areas.

Brunswick officials said they had been tracking the Karenia mikimotoi bloom in Casco Bay since early September and observed stressed or dying clams in several locations. The town says the species does not produce the kind of toxin that threatens people who eat shellfish; at high concentrations, it can harm marine organisms and contribute to low oxygen in the water.

In Brunswick, officials reported that about 80% of adult clams in affected areas showed extreme stress, were dying or were already dead, according to Maine Public’s account of the department’s findings. The town had initially asked harvesters to avoid visibly affected flats while it assessed conditions; state closures now prohibit harvesting in designated areas.

The closures carry economic weight for the coastal communities. Brunswick was Maine’s largest soft-shell clam port in 2025, with nearly $1.8 million in reported landings, Maine Public said, citing state records. Harvesters should check Maine’s Department of Marine Resources closure notices for the current boundaries and status before digging.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Maine closes Casco Bay clam flats after algal bloom
seoDescription: Maine closed shellfish harvesting in parts of Maquoit and Middle bays after an algal bloom was linked to severe clam stress and die-off.
